content.text: Some thoughts upon initial review of the current state of Fedora's authz stack:
We will remove support for the deprecated XACML and RBACL Fedora Authorization Delegates (FADs)

Confirm what happens if we initialize Modeshape without a FAD; if it defaults to full access, that's fine, otherwise we may need to have a simple FAD to just grant full access to any operation that has bee cleared by the HTTP layer
Remove the AbstractRolesAuthorizationDelegate class and any related cruft from the WebAC FAD
Investigate rewriting the WebAC FAD to use Apache Shiro, and use the Shiro API in the HTTP layer

Per some discussion on tech calls in recent weeks, I will be using this ticket as the jumping off point for doing a sweep through the fcrepo-auth-* code to look for code that should be removed or deprecated.
Current work-in-progress of removing unused code:
:  I'm assigning this one to you and moving it to "In Progress" since it sounds like you are moving forward on it.

I have marked some more classes as deprecated in fcrepo-auth-common. However, I will not be able to remove one of the main ones, ServletContainerAuthenticationProvider, until the principal provider integration tests are rewritten to not rely on that class.
Per discussion in #tech, I have gone ahead and removed the ITs from fcrepo-auth-common. The principal providers can be integration tested as part of the fcrepo-auth-webac integration tests.

Currently there is a mismatch between Mode and WebAC permission modes which makes it difficult to implement SOLID/WAC features such as acl:Append.  More precisely,  WebAC permissions are more granular than Modeshape.    The work of this ticket (which may need to be broken into multiple tickets depending on what is involved) move WebAC into the fcrepo-http-api layer.

comments.body:
Some thoughts upon initial review of the current state of Fedora's authz stack:

  1. We will remove support for the deprecated XACML and RBACL Fedora Authorization Delegates (FADs)
  2. Confirm what happens if we initialize Modeshape without a FAD; if it defaults to full access, that's fine, otherwise we may need to have a simple FAD to just grant full access to any operation that has bee cleared by the HTTP layer
  3. Remove the AbstractRolesAuthorizationDelegate class and any related cruft from the WebAC FAD
  4. Investigate rewriting the WebAC FAD to use Apache Shiro, and use the Shiro API in the HTTP layer

Shiro implementation pseudocode sketch:

class WebACAuthorizingRealm extends AuthorizingRealm {
  doGetAuthorizationInfo(prinicpals) {
    List<WebACPermission> permissions = ...
    return new WebACAuthorizationInfo(permissions)
  }
}

class FedoraLdp {
  someMethod(request) {
    mode = methodToMode(request)
    resource = requestToResource(request)
    subject.checkPermission(new WebACPermission(resource, mode)
    ...
  }
}

Per some discussion on tech calls in recent weeks, I will be using this ticket as the jumping off point for doing a sweep through the fcrepo-auth-* code to look for code that should be removed or deprecated.
Current work-in-progress of removing unused code: https://github.com/peichman-umd/fcrepo4/tree/webac-cleanup
Peter Matthew Eichman:  I'm assigning this one to you and moving it to "In Progress" since it sounds like you are moving forward on it.

I have marked some more classes as deprecated in fcrepo-auth-common. However, I will not be able to remove one of the main ones, ServletContainerAuthenticationProvider, until the principal provider integration tests are rewritten to not rely on that class.
Per discussion in #tech, I have gone ahead and removed the ITs from fcrepo-auth-common. The principal providers can be integration tested as part of the fcrepo-auth-webac integration tests.
